standard_prerequisites.name: A scheme locally of finite type over a Jacobson scheme is Jacobson
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-Jacobson-universally-Jacobson, invoked at proof line 1475
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that closed points are dense in every closed subset and map to closed points of the base, so that a chain of irreducible closed subsets may be ended with a closed point.

standard_prerequisites.name: The dimension of a scheme through the dimensions of its local rings, and finiteness of the residue field extension at a closed point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties, label properties-lemma-codimension-local-ring (proof line 1480); Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points (proof line 1486)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first expresses the dimension as the supremum of the dimensions of the local rings at the closed points, and the second makes the residue field extension at a closed point finite.

core_obligations: Reduce to closed points: since the source is Jacobson, closed points of an integral closed subscheme are dense and map to closed points of the base, so the dimension of the subscheme is the supremum of the dimensions of its local rings at closed points (proof lines 1471-1481).

Compute the local dimension: the dimension of the local ring at a closed point equals the difference of the dimension function values at the generic point and at that point, by the properties of a dimension function (proof lines 1482-1483).

Conclude: the residue field extension at a closed point is finite, so the relative dimension function vanishes there because the base point has dimension zero; hence the dimension of the local ring equals the relative dimension of the generic point, and all three integers agree (proof lines 1484-1488).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to closed points via the Jacobson property (proof lines 1471-1481).
Local dimension as a difference of dimension function values (proof lines 1482-1483).
Vanishing of the relative dimension function at closed points and conclusion (proof lines 1484-1488).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a Jacobson base whose closed points have dimension zero, the relative dimension function at the generic point of an integral subscheme, the dimension of that subscheme and the dimension of its local ring at a closed point all agree (statement lines 1457-1469, tag 02QK-adjacent). The proof uses the Jacobson property to reduce to closed points, expresses the dimension as a supremum of local ring dimensions, rewrites those as differences of dimension function values, and observes that at closed points the relative dimension function vanishes because the residue field extension is finite and the base point has dimension zero. The Jacobson reduction and the vanishing at closed points are the substance, so the claim is H2.
